note: Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion `orb validate` (the Rust validator) reports for the same program, filtered to this rule's codes at entity-directive paths. The first three cases copy entity_access.rs tests intrinsic_field_in_access_policy_errors, persisted_field_in_access_policy_passes and unknown_field_in_access_policy_is_unaffected_by_the_intrinsic_rule, and the next seven copy the owner_columns_scoped_tests (flags_owner_column_with_no_read_policy, silent_once_read_is_declared, silent_for_an_app_declaring_no_identity_entity_at_all, does_not_guess_from_a_field_name_a_bare_string_owner_is_invisible, flags_the_omission_when_nothing_declares_it, goes_quiet_once_read_none_reason_declares_it, a_waiver_on_a_different_operation_does_not_silence_read). The rest pin branches those tests leave open: the binding roots, the object/get call form, owner typing in both operand orders, the role vocabulary through =, !=, array/includes (list, bare, field and dynamic haystacks), the identity requirement and its expects exemption, policy-derived and collection-mirror owner columns, a self-identity id column, an auxiliary entity, intrinsic relations, and path order across directives and orbitals. The @user.<field> existence checks are not ported (no lint input carries the Viewer members), so no case reads an undeclared @user field.

findings.message: `Note.@update[1]` reads `@entity.isEditing`, an @intrinsic field of entity `Note` — intrinsic fields are trait-owned view-state, never seeded or persisted by the runtime, so using one as an access-policy input is a bypassable gate.
findings.suggestion: Base this access directive on a real persisted field of `Note`, not the @intrinsic field `isEditing`.

findings.message: `@entity.bogus` is not a field of entity `Note`. It resolves to null, so this access directive silently denies everyone.
findings.suggestion: Declare `bogus` on entity Note, or read one of: id, isEditing, ownerId

findings.message: Ticket declares owner column(s) `assignee` pointing at the [identity] entity, but no @read directive — and an undeclared policy is ALLOW-ALL, not deny-all, so every viewer reads every row
findings.suggestion: declare @read on Ticket scoping rows to the viewer, e.g. @read ["=", (object/get @entity assignee), @user.id] — or, when visibility genuinely depends on a DIFFERENT entity (a membership/enrolment join a per-row predicate cannot express), omit @read and state that reason in a comment on the entity, citing R-ENTITY-ACCESS-NO-COLLECTION-AGGREGATE-BINDING

findings.message: `@payload` is not a legal binding inside an access directive — only `@entity` (the candidate row) and `@user` (the viewer) are. Access directives have no call site, so `@payload`/`@config`/`@state` are not meaningful here.
findings.suggestion: Read only @entity.<field> or @user.<field>.

findings.message: `Ticket.customerEmail` is compared to `@user.id` but is not a relation to the [identity] entity `Person` — it is `string`. Viewer ids are only ever stamped onto declared relations, so this predicate matches no row and the directive denies everyone.
findings.suggestion: Type `customerEmail` as a relation to Person (`customerEmail : Person`), or compare against the field the viewer value actually lives in

findings.message: `@read` on entity `Note` reads `@user`, but this program declares no [identity] entity. An access directive needs a real roster to resolve against — declare `[identity]` on the entity that models your app's viewer.
findings.suggestion: Tag your user-directory entity `[persistent: <collection>, identity]`.
